facts.statement: Cosmacanthus is an extinct genus of placoderms belonging to the family Groenlandaspididae.
facts.quote: Cosmacanthus is an extinct genus of placoderms in the extinct family Groenlandaspididae

facts.statement: The genus Cosmacanthus was named by Louis Agassiz in 1845.
facts.quote: It was named by Louis Agassiz in 1845.

facts.statement: Cosmacanthus lived during the Late Devonian in Ireland, the UK, Russia, and North America.
facts.quote: Cosmacanthus is an extinct genus of placoderms in the extinct family Groenlandaspididae that lived during the Late Devonian in Ireland, the UK, Russia and North America.

facts.statement: Cosmacanthus lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)

facts.statement: Cosmacanthus belongs to the parent group Arthrodira.
Cosmacanthus is classified in the class Placodermi.
There are five recorded fossil occurrences of Cosmacanthus in the Paleobiology Database.
The genus Cosmacanthus includes several species such as C. bullatus, C. carinatus, C. malcolmsoni, C. marginalis, C. priscus, C. sellatus, and C. semistriatus.
